title: Rehearse a Small Repair
status: New proposed Lesson 07 production script, 2026-10-30. No new animation or narration in this handoff.
learningOutcome: Privately rehearse one task-linked next move after a brief pause, leaving space for the actual reply and avoiding claims that the plan or discussion is already resolved.

scenario.kind: Original fictional discussion training with independent resettable excerpts
scenario.sourcePrompt: A community centre wants a 20-minute welcome activity for new members. Help them meet one another and find out about its weekly drawing group. Your group should recommend one activity and explain how it serves both aims. Use the main room and existing paper and pens; do not buy anything.

facts.text: The required output is one recommended welcome activity and an explanation of how it serves both aims.
The welcome activity lasts 20 minutes, in the main room, using existing paper and pens without purchases.
The aims are helping new members meet one another and find out about the weekly drawing group.
Maya's initial proposal is: We could start in pairs and exchange names and interests.
Noah's separate proposal is: We could each draw or write one thing we'd like to try, then use that to introduce ourselves.
No option has been adopted and no activity has taken place. Proposal replies do not establish agreement or successful results.
Each section declares a fresh excerpt or reset. A pause, overlap, invitation or sidetrack in one excerpt is not evidence that a character has a fixed personality.

unknowns: Why any participant pauses or speaks less
How many new members will attend
The drawing group's specific programme beyond its weekly occurrence
Which proposal the group will eventually adopt

pause.baseline: Maya has just offered F04. A short pause follows. Noah has not yet responded to that proposal. The cause of the pause is unknown.
pause.timingMeaning: A chosen illustration interval, not a universal threshold for intervening.

overlap.baseline: Fresh excerpt. The learner begins to connect paired introductions to the weekly drawing group. Noah begins F05 before the learner finishes. Only the start of that proposal is presented in the overlap baseline; its full content becomes available if a branch invites him to continue.
overlap.pendingLearnerPoint: After exchanging names, pairs could identify one question about the weekly drawing group.
overlap.clipDesign: The silent review shows an explicitly marked two-lane overlap illustration. Do not infer speech interruption from silence or fake audio. Later voice production must deliberately verify any overlap timing and intelligibility.

invitation.baseline: Fresh excerpt with F04 and F05 available as unadopted proposals. Maya has not yet commented on their comparison. The learner can offer an open invitation with permission to pass; no private motive is assigned.

sidetrack.baseline: Fresh excerpt. While discussing the welcome activity, Noah asks: The centre's old sign looks dated. Which lettering style would be better? This is an authored side topic, not a verified fact about a real centre.
sidetrack.boundary: A design topic is not inherently irrelevant. Ask whether it helps the stated welcome task; do not infer laziness or assign blame.

rehearsal.baseline: Fresh excerpt. Maya offers F04; a brief pause follows and no one has linked the idea to the weekly drawing group yet. Rehearse one possible next move, not a final recommendation.
rehearsal.boundary: Any model peer reply is separately authored and does not respond to the learner's unheard speech.

boundaries: No universal silence duration, speaking quota, obligatory leader role or guaranteed polite-phrase effect.
A pause may be useful; an overlap may be accidental. Use observable words and timing, not mind-reading.
An invitation allows passing or later participation; do not force a quiet participant to explain themselves.
Repair one immediate difficulty, then leave space and respond to what actually follows.
No live speech detection, microphone, scoring, emotion detection or automatic evaluation.
The 20-minute activity is a scenario constraint, not the discussion time limit or the course runtime.
Short scenario dialogue is subordinate to formal animated explanation; no permanent three-person skit.

blocks.title: Choose a Move That Fits the Gap
Try the Line and Leave Space
Use the Reply You Actually Get

L07.S06.c001.speaker: coach
L07.S06.c001.text: You do not need to repair a whole discussion in one turn. A useful next move can identify a missing link, ask a manageable question, or give someone room to continue. Choose what the moment needs instead of trying to demonstrate every technique at once.
L07.S06.c001.visualEn: Open on optional repair resources, not a compulsory sequence or leader role. Formal animated cards carry the explanation.
L07.S06.c001.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L07.S06.c001.delivery: Calm, concrete teaching; emphasis follows the semantic distinction, with natural pauses.

L07.S06.c002.speaker: coach
L07.S06.c002.text: This rehearsal starts from a fresh excerpt. The group is considering the twenty-minute welcome activity in the main room, using existing paper and pens. Both aims still matter: meeting one another and finding out about the weekly drawing group. No proposal has been adopted.
L07.S06.c002.visualEn: Explicit reset to S06. Clear all earlier invitation, overlap, sidetrack and authored replies. Keep the exact source prompt readable in a separate reference panel. The 20 minutes labels the activity only.
L07.S06.c002.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L07.S06.c002.delivery: Calm, concrete teaching; emphasis follows the semantic distinction, with natural pauses.

L07.S06.d001.speaker: maya
L07.S06.d001.text: We could start in pairs and exchange names and interests.
L07.S06.d001.visualEn: Present exact F04 as the only current proposal speech. Maya’s delivery is neutral; no discouragement or impatience is inferred.
L07.S06.d001.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L07.S06.d001.delivery: Natural collaborative speech; restrained gesture, no exaggerated conflict or comic voice.

L07.S06.c003.speaker: coach
L07.S06.c003.text: A brief pause follows. We do not know why. In this excerpt, nobody has yet connected the paired introduction to the weekly drawing group. That gives you a particular gap to consider, without needing to diagnose how anyone feels or decide that silence itself is a problem.
L07.S06.c003.visualEn: Use a neutral pause marker, then the missing second-goal relation. Do not assign motives, personality traits or agreement to any cast member.
L07.S06.c003.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L07.S06.c003.delivery: Calm, concrete teaching; emphasis follows the semantic distinction, with natural pauses.

L07.S06.c004.speaker: coach
L07.S06.c004.text: You could build on Maya’s idea by asking about that second aim. You could also leave a little space if someone seems about to continue, without claiming to know their intention. There is no rule that a certain number of quiet seconds means you must take over.
L07.S06.c004.visualEn: Show optional Wait and Ask about the link resources. Use visible turn space without an inferred intention detector. No automatic intervention after h100 or assigned leadership.
L07.S06.c004.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L07.S06.c004.delivery: Calm, concrete teaching; emphasis follows the semantic distinction, with natural pauses.

L07.S06.c005.speaker: coach
L07.S06.c005.text: For this rehearsal, prepare one short line that would help examine the missing link. Keep it connected to the proposal already offered. You are not choosing a final activity, making up the drawing group’s programme, or promising that every new member will learn about it.
L07.S06.c005.visualEn: Show the exact F04 card beside the two goals and a blank private area. Hide all model lines; no invented weekly programme or information provider.
L07.S06.c005.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L07.S06.c005.delivery: Calm, concrete teaching; emphasis follows the semantic distinction, with natural pauses.

L07.S06.c006.speaker: coach
L07.S06.c006.text: Try the line in English. You can say it aloud, write it privately, or think it through. This is private practice, with no recording or scoring. Aim for something the group could respond to, then leave a little space instead of immediately answering your own question.
L07.S06.c006.visualEn: Show one privacy note and a blank private workspace. No microphone, transcript, AI judgement or saved response; the model stays hidden.
L07.S06.c006.anchorHint: instead of immediately answering your own question
L07.S06.c006.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L07.S06.c006.delivery: Calm, concrete teaching; emphasis follows the semantic distinction, with natural pauses.

L07.S06.c007.speaker: coach
L07.S06.c007.text: Watch gives you thirty-five seconds, then shows one example and continues automatically. Practice waits for you to see the model or skip it. In Practice, after the model you can try again or continue. The example is one possibility, not the only useful response.
L07.S06.c007.visualEn: Prepare I03 controls as readable DOM outside the stage. Watch automatically follows the authored model and rejoins; Practice waits without timeout. Keep personal and authored-model areas separate.
L07.S06.c007.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L07.S06.c007.delivery: Calm, concrete teaching; emphasis follows the semantic distinction, with natural pauses.

L07.S06.c008.speaker: coach
L07.S06.c008.text: Check whether your next move responds to what was actually said and gives the group a manageable question. If you did not make an attempt, keep those checks for later. You do not have to supply the final activity before making a useful contribution.
L07.S06.c008.visualEn: Immediate common continuation for model and skip routes. No assumption that a learner spoke, saw the model, succeeded or chose a final plan.
L07.S06.c008.anchorHint: If you did not make an attempt
L07.S06.c008.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L07.S06.c008.delivery: Calm, concrete teaching; emphasis follows the semantic distinction, with natural pauses.

L07.S06.c009.speaker: coach
L07.S06.c009.text: What comes next depends on the reply. Someone might suggest a connection, ask for clarification, or still need time. Attend to that response rather than forcing your prepared follow-up. A question that sounds polite does not guarantee agreement or a smooth continuation.
L07.S06.c009.visualEn: Show possible next-response categories as conditional options, not enacted outcomes. No prediction that Noah or Maya will respond in a particular way outside the authored model.
L07.S06.c009.anchorHint: rather than forcing your prepared follow-up
L07.S06.c009.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L07.S06.c009.delivery: Calm, concrete teaching; emphasis follows the semantic distinction, with natural pauses.

L07.S06.c010.speaker: coach
L07.S06.c010.text: For another attempt, choose one small change: name the missing aim more clearly, shorten a question with several demands, or remove an assumption about the group. Keep your line open enough for someone else to develop it. You can leave a useful problem unresolved.
L07.S06.c010.visualEn: Provide optional private revision cues. Do not create a required three-part formula, an additional gate or automatic model-matching evaluation.
L07.S06.c010.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L07.S06.c010.delivery: Calm, concrete teaching; emphasis follows the semantic distinction, with natural pauses.

L07.S06.c011.speaker: coach
L07.S06.c011.text: A small repair gives the group a place to continue. Offer it, leave space, and notice what follows. The eventual recommendation still needs to serve both aims within the activity’s conditions; this short contribution does not settle that wider decision.
L07.S06.c011.visualEn: Close with the shared task and its two aims still open. Normal replay controls only; no adopted-plan stamp, mastery badge or automatic navigation.
L07.S06.c011.anchorHint: does not settle that wider decision
L07.S06.c011.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L07.S06.c011.delivery: Calm, concrete teaching; emphasis follows the semantic distinction, with natural pauses.

L07.S06.d101.speaker: learner
L07.S06.d101.text: The paired introductions could help people meet. How could they also help members find out about the weekly drawing group?
L07.S06.d101.visualEn: Show One possible next move in a distinct authored-model frame. Point to the possible first-goal link and the missing second-goal link; neither is a demonstrated result.
L07.S06.d101.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L07.S06.d101.delivery: Natural collaborative speech; restrained gesture, no exaggerated conflict or comic voice.

L07.S06.d102.speaker: noah
L07.S06.d102.text: Pairs could write one question about the group. We would still need to check where the answers would come from.
L07.S06.d102.visualEn: Noah makes a limited proposal inside the authored model. Do not invent a facilitator, available expert, programme details or a source already checked. The activity remains undecided.
L07.S06.d102.anchorHint: where the answers would come from
L07.S06.d102.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L07.S06.d102.delivery: Natural collaborative speech; restrained gesture, no exaggerated conflict or comic voice.

L07.S06.f101.speaker: coach
L07.S06.f101.text: The next move picks up Maya’s idea and draws attention to the missing aim. Noah’s suggestion makes the information question more specific. Writing a question does not yet tell visitors about the group; an answer source still needs checking. The model leaves that work open rather than finishing the plan.
L07.S06.f101.visualEn: Return to a formal analysis board. Keep question generation separate from obtaining answers and from the goal being achieved. No repair-success, agreement or activity-completion badge.
L07.S06.f101.anchorHint: an answer source still needs checking
L07.S06.f101.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L07.S06.f101.delivery: Calm, concrete teaching; emphasis follows the semantic distinction, with natural pauses.

L07.S06.h100.purpose: Present the brief pause in this authored excerpt before analysing it.
L07.S06.h100.visualEn: Keep the proposal and two aims visible for a three-second illustration only. Do not display a countdown, detected-silence warning, urgency or universal intervention threshold.

L07.S06.h101.purpose: Privately identify the gap and choose a task-linked next move.
L07.S06.h101.visualEn: Keep the private area blank and the exact proposal accessible; no response or understanding is inferred.

L07.S06.h102.purpose: Privately revise one feature of the next move if useful.
L07.S06.h102.visualEn: The private area stays blank; no speaking, repair success, agreement or completion is inferred.

L07.I03.prompt: After Maya’s proposal and the brief pause, rehearse one English next move that helps examine the missing connection to the weekly drawing group.
L07.I03.skipNote: Continue to the shared explanation without assuming a response or a successful repair.

boundary: Use formal explanation and short explicitly fictional excerpts. A pause does not establish consent or a motive. Model replies are authored possibilities, not observed student speech or guaranteed effects.
